clue.text: Game birds follow their leader

indicators.note: follow says the birds come after their leader in the answer

parts.note: the leader of the birds is the first letter of the word birds, a B
owls are birds

explanation.surface: Game birds trail obediently behind the one at the front of the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game birds' reads as one phrase, but 'Game' alone is the definition. 'Their leader' is the B that heads 'birds'; OWLS follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowls is a sport played on a green by rolling weighted balls towards a jack.

clue.text: Drink to, blue-stocking, perhaps, from Israel town

parts.note: beer is a drink
a bluestocking is an educated woman, and a woman who is a Bachelor of Arts is a SHE who is a BA

explanation.surface: Raise a toast to an intellectual woman from a town in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: A bluestocking is a learned, literary woman; a female arts graduate fits, read as SHE plus BA.
explanation.definitionFit: Beersheba is a city in the Negev desert in southern Israel.

clue.text: We introduce Henry, the big swimmer

indicators.note: introduce means put inside, so the word We takes Henry into its middle

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: We present Henry, the large champion swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduce' looks like a social introduction but means insert.
explanation.definitionFit: A whale is a huge sea mammal, the largest animal that swims.

clue.text: 20 decamping?

definitions.meaning: the answer to 20 down, a ship's or team's commander
one who decamps or skips off could playfully be called this

explanation.walkthrough: 20 is CAPTAIN; the second definition coins a noun from skip, to run away.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain of a boat or team is also called by this name, and someone skipping away is fancifully one too.

clue.text: Those notes mislaid by Sullivan ?

parts.note: Arthur Sullivan's famous Victorian song tells of a musician who struck a wonderful chord once and could never find it again

explanation.surface: A composer has misplaced some music.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Arthur Sullivan, of Gilbert and Sullivan, wrote the parlour song whose title this is; 'notes' are musical, not written ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's title names a chord, a group of notes, that the player loses and searches for in vain.

clue.text: Concealed deceased, not being heartless

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king

indicators.note: heartless means losing its middle, so the word not loses its centre letter

explanation.surface: A secret dead man, who was not without feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle O out of 'not', leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Latent means present but hidden, not yet developed or visible.

clue.text: Said the piano needs repair, in a minor way

indicators.note: something needing repair must be put back together, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Someone said the piano needed fixing, in a small way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs repair' rearranges SAID, THE and P (piano). 'in a minor way' looks like 'slightly' but 'a minor way' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A side-path is a small track branching off a main road.

clue.text: Might fall for a bit of mischief?

parts.note: can and might both express possibility or permission
a trip is a stumble or fall

explanation.surface: Someone might tumble for the sake of a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantrip is a Scots word for a witch's spell or a playful trick.

clue.text: Regulation formerly made about drain construction

indicators.note: made about means set round, so the word for formerly encloses the rest

parts.note: once means formerly, at one time

indicators.note: construction means building, so the letters of drain are put together anew

explanation.surface: A rule from the past was made about building drains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' is the anagram signal and 'made about' the container signal; the surface reads them as building work on a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative decree or official rule.

clue.text: Laundry error includes a towel, perhaps

indicators.note: includes says the letters sit within the words Laundry error

explanation.surface: A laundry mistake takes in a towel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a towel, perhaps' defines by example: a towel dries things.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is one example of something used to dry, so it can be called by this name.

clue.text: Came back with a diet scheme, appearing very thin

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word Came from right to left
a scheme is a plan or arrangement, so the letters of a diet are set out anew

explanation.surface: Someone returned on a diet plan looking dangerously gaunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CAME into EMAC; 'scheme' rearranges A DIET into IATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be emaciated is to be abnormally thin from lack of food.

clue.text: Simpleton demands rum in New York

indicators.note: in places the strange word inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: rum in British slang means odd or strange

explanation.surface: A fool asks for a glass of rum while in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like a drink but is the adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A noddy is an old word for a fool or dimwit.

clue.text: Retired business-man?

parts.note: read retired as gone to bed: a business partner who takes no active part could be called one who is asleep

explanation.surface: A man who has stepped back from business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests no longer working, but here it means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner who invests money in a firm but takes no part in running it is jokingly said to be dozing.

clue.text: Whole of northern territory in the country

indicators.note: in puts the territory's letters inside the country's name

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland, the country
NT is the abbreviation for Australia's Northern Territory

explanation.surface: All of an Australian territory lying within one nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means complete or whole, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Avoid committing oneself regarding time to get up

parts.note: tempo is time or speed in music
to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Avoid making a commitment about when to get out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to delay or stall in order to gain time.

clue.text: Payments for the cloth ?

parts.note: the cloth is a name for the clergy, so these are the salaries paid to clergymen rather than the price of fabric

explanation.surface: Money paid for some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' is the clergy, and a stipend is a vicar's salary.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergymen receive fixed regular salaries known by this name.

clue.text: Is in Leeds, arranging subsidiary activities

indicators.note: arranging means putting in a new order, so the letters of Is in Leeds are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone in Leeds is organising minor pursuits on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' rearranges IS IN LEEDS. Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidelines are activities pursued in addition to a main job.

clue.text: Odd gins after one for the road here?

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters of gins are mixed

parts.note: post is a Latin prefix meaning after

explanation.surface: Peculiar gins after a final drink for the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one for the road' suggests a last drink, but here it is something that stands by the road. 'Odd' rearranges GINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost is a marker standing by the road to direct travellers.

clue.text: Stirring march tune for such sedentary strategists ?

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of march are jumbled

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A rousing military march for generals who direct battles from their seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' looks like praise for the march but rearranges MARCH into ARMCH. The answer describes strategists who theorise from a comfortable chair.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic or strategist pronounces on matters without practical experience, seated at home.

clue.text: Hothead feels some irritation with temporary stoppages

parts.note: the head of the word hot is its first letter, H
itches means feels a slight irritation

explanation.surface: An angry person is irritated by brief delays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hothead' looks like a quick-tempered person but splits as the head of 'hot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitches are minor problems that briefly hold things up.

clue.text: Long effusion shows direction to a system of belief

parts.note: S for south is a compass direction
a creed is a system of religious belief

explanation.surface: A lengthy outpouring setting someone on the way to a faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long, often tedious piece of writing or speech.

clue.text: Industry's leader is able to hold a pit assembly

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the word for is able goes round the rest

parts.note: can means is able

indicators.note: assembly means putting parts together, so the letters of a pit are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A company boss manages to hold a meeting of coal miners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' looks like a gathering of miners but is the anagram signal; 'to hold' is the container signal. A captain of industry is a business leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain of industry is a leading business figure.

clue.text: Entrant has had it!

parts.note: had it sounds like ruined, but it means simply possessed: anyone who has entered must have been granted the way in

explanation.surface: Someone joining is done for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has had it' reads as slang for being finished; literally, an entrant has received the right of entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission or the right to enter is what every entrant must have been given.

clue.text: Just the money to save the sinking fund ?

definitions.text: Just the money to save the sinking fund ?

parts.words: Just the money to save the sinking fund ?
parts.note: money that stays on the surface would rescue a fund that is going under; in finance the term means capital in circulation rather than fixed

explanation.surface: Exactly the cash needed to rescue a failing investment fund.
explanation.walkthrough: A sinking fund is a real financial term for money set aside to repay a debt; the clue reads it literally as a fund going under.
explanation.definitionFit: Circulating money, as opposed to fixed assets, is described with a word meaning staying on the surface of water.

clue.text: Old prison ships?

definitions.meaning: a notorious London debtors' prison, closed in the nineteenth century
a number of ships sailing together form a navy's squadron

explanation.walkthrough: The Fleet Prison stood by the Fleet river in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic London jail had this name, and a group of ships under one command has it too.

clue.text: Article 9 has note added

parts.note: 9 refers to the answer to 9 across, meaning very thin, which here gives thin
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Clause nine has an extra note appended.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' points to 9 across, whose definition is 'very thin'; THIN with the note G added.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is an object or item, much as an article is.

clue.text: Choice about period and method of working.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for choice goes round the period

parts.note: an option is a choice
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A selection concerning a period of time and a way of doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal: the word for choice is split open to take the period.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a process or way in which something works.

clue.text: The eccentric sister of a Greek at Troy

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of the and sister are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd sibling of a Greek soldier at the siege of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges THE SISTER. Thersites is the foul-mouthed common soldier in Homer's Iliad.
explanation.definitionFit: Thersites is the ugly, abusive Greek soldier in Homer's Iliad who mocks Agamemnon at the siege.

clue.text: Asian tribesmen like chasing a horse

indicators.note: chasing means running behind, so like comes after the horse

parts.note: a nag is a horse, especially an old one
as means like, in the sense of in the manner of

explanation.surface: Asian tribesmen are compared to someone running after a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nagas are a group of hill peoples of north-east India and Myanmar.
